question.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the fractional term $-\frac{2x}{3}$ by subtracting $\frac{5}{2}$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{2x}{3}+\frac{5}{2} & =4 \\ -\frac{2x}{3}+\frac{5}{2}-\frac{5}{2} & =\frac{8}{2}-\frac{5}{2} \\ -\frac{2x}{3} & =\frac{8-5}{2} \\ -\frac{2x}{3} & =\frac{3}{2} \\ -\frac{2x}{3} & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The fractional coefficient is $-\frac{2}{3},$ so we multiply by its reciprocal ${(-\frac{2}{3})}^{-1}=-\frac{3}{2}.$ This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2}\cdot (-\frac{2x}{3}) & =-\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2} \\ 1x & =-\frac{9}{4} \\ x & =-\frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
